paa_questions.question: What is the Dogfight Position in BJJ?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Dynamic half guard variation where both practitioners are up on their knees facing each other in an underhook battle
paa_questions.rationale: Primary definition question - should be front-loaded in overview with conversational heading

paa_questions.question: How do you get to Dogfight from half guard?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Establish underhook from flat half guard, elevate hips off mat, come up to knees while maintaining frames
paa_questions.rationale: Entry mechanics are in prerequisites but need dedicated 'How to Enter' section

paa_questions.question: What are the best sweeps from Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Old School Sweep (70% advanced), Back Take (65% advanced), Deep Half Entry (75% advanced)
paa_questions.rationale: Success-focused query - create comparison table of sweep options with success rates

paa_questions.question: Why is it called the Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: The term describes the scrambling, competitive nature where both players vie for dominant grips like dogs fighting
paa_questions.rationale: Etymology question adds context - brief sidebar or callout in overview

paa_questions.question: How do you defend against Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Whizzer control (55% success), crossface pressure, flatten opponent with smash pass (50% success)
paa_questions.rationale: Top player perspective - defensive_responses should have conversational heading

paa_questions.question: What's the difference between Dogfight and regular half guard?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Dogfight is elevated on knees with underhook battle, while flat half guard has bottom player on back
paa_questions.rationale: Comparison question - needs explicit comparison section near overview

paa_questions.question: When should I use Dogfight Position instead of Deep Half?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Use Dogfight when you have space to elevate and want aggressive back takes; Deep Half when opponent applies heavy pressure
paa_questions.rationale: Strategic decision-making query - FAQ section at bottom

paa_questions.question: What are common mistakes in Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Allowing opponent to flatten you, staying static, losing underhook battle, dropping head too low
paa_questions.rationale: Already has common_errors section but heading should be conversational

paa_questions.question: How long can you stay in Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: 30-90 seconds typically - highly dynamic position resolves quickly to sweep, back take, or pass
paa_questions.rationale: Time-based query - position_metrics data should be surfaced earlier

paa_questions.question: Is Dogfight Position good for beginners?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Challenging for beginners (45% retention rate) but teaches essential underhook battles and frames
paa_questions.rationale: Skill level appropriateness - add 'For Which Skill Levels?' callout

paa_questions.question: What submissions can you do from Dogfight?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Electric Chair (50% advanced), chained through Back Control for RNC, or sweep to Mount for armbars
paa_questions.rationale: Submission-focused query - highlight optimal_submission_paths more prominently

paa_questions.question: How do you maintain underhook in Dogfight?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Drive forward pressure constantly, keep head high, never voluntarily give space or pull backward
paa_questions.rationale: Technical detail query - extract from key_principles into dedicated subsection

paa_questions.question: What does Gordon Ryan say about Dogfight Position?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Gordon Ryan: 'One of my favorite half guard positions because it's inherently aggressive and threatens back take first'
paa_questions.rationale: Authority/expert query - expert_insights already exists but heading could be more specific

paa_questions.question: Can you use Dogfight in gi BJJ or just no-gi?
paa_questions.answer_snippet: Works in both gi and no-gi but especially dynamic in no-gi where lack of grips creates faster scrambles
paa_questions.rationale: Context specification - add brief 'Gi vs No-Gi Considerations' note

paa_questions.question: What's the success rate of Old School Sweep from Dogfight?
paa_questions.rationale: Specific data query - success rates should be in scannable format with visual emphasis
